title: Watch Your Back With Sin
verse: And the Lord sent a plague on the people because they had made the calf—the one Aaron made.
observation: Many people have criticized the Hebrews for turning away from God so quickly. It is possible to also give Aaron a hard time for allowing them to do so. However, it is important to realize they had heard of the calf-god Baal their entire lives, and they had likely heard of his “power” over and over. Even though they had witnessed the amazing power of Yahweh, they were still conditioned in ways they had not yet broken free from. When we turn to God, we must be careful about our past sins and old ways of living. Until we become more mature in our walk with God, sin will often try to entice and confuse us. We can forget the slavery of Egypt and only see the momentary peace it offers. Be careful not to let sin lie to you. The moment of pleasure it offers comes with lifelong chains. However, patient faithfulness with Yahweh brings joy that lasts for all eternity.
application: Is there an old sin constantly whispering to you? Remind yourself that it comes with chains and wait for the LORD.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking us out of every dark place and being worth the wait.
